_readme: UPGRADE_PLAN_V6 C1 (2026-11-15): real astronauts as the ship's crew. FACTS ONLY, never invented dialogue: press E next to a crew member and a narrator tells these sourced facts (the person never 'speaks'). Every fact has a NASA source link, checked on 2026-11-15. An entry with "show": false is hidden (the PLACEHOLDER slot). look = how their toy figure looks (skin, hair_style, hair_color, suit_color, older, beard, camera). missions = the crew on each mission (the same three people for the whole mission). The game also says one honest line: our crew is a game-design choice.
game_choice_line: On this mission, {name} is part of your crew. That part is our game's idea: the facts above are real.

ride.name: Sally Ride
facts: On June 18, 1983, Sally Ride became the first American woman in space, on space shuttle mission STS-7.
She was picked in NASA's 1978 astronaut class, the first class to include women.
She flew again in 1984 on STS-41G, and later became a professor at the University of California, San Diego.

koch.name: Christina Koch
koch.one_line: Record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman
facts: Christina Koch spent 328 days in space on the International Space Station: the longest single spaceflight by a woman.
On that mission she made six spacewalks, including the first all-woman spacewalks.
On April 1, 2026, she launched on Artemis II, the crewed flight around the Moon.

glover.name: Victor Glover
glover.one_line: Pilot of Artemis II and SpaceX Crew-1
facts: Victor Glover is a NASA astronaut and U.S. Navy test pilot, picked by NASA in 2013.
He was the pilot of SpaceX Crew-1 and lived on the space station for 168 days, making four spacewalks.
He was the pilot of Artemis II, which launched on April 1, 2026 and flew around the Moon.

whitson.name: Peggy Whitson
whitson.one_line: Most total days in space of any American
facts: Peggy Whitson holds the U.S. record for the most total time in space: more days than any other American astronaut.
In 2008 she became the first woman to command the International Space Station, and later the first woman to command it twice.
She is a biochemist, and she flew to the station again in 2025 on Axiom Mission 4.

mann.name: Nicole Mann
mann.one_line: First Native American woman in space
facts: Nicole Mann became the first Native American woman in space when she launched on October 5, 2022.
She was the commander of NASA's SpaceX Crew-5, and spent 157 days in orbit.
She is a U.S. Marine Corps test pilot, and she is registered with the Wailacki of the Round Valley Indian Tribes.

pettit.name: Don Pettit
pettit.one_line: Space station scientist and space photographer
facts: Don Pettit is a NASA scientist-astronaut who has flown four spaceflights and spent 590 days in space.
He is famous for his photos from the space station: on his last stay he took more than 670,000 pictures.
He invents science in his spare time: he made the first 'space cup' to drink from in zero-g.

glenn.name: John Glenn
facts: On February 20, 1962, John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth, going around three times in Friendship 7.
He was one of NASA's first seven astronauts, the Mercury 7.
In 1998, at age 77, he flew to space again on space shuttle Discovery (STS-95).
